content.text:
The current wheel selects four ranking boards. It does not show individual entities or declaration categories. `/rankings` initially selects MPs. Clicking MPs, Individuals, Companies or Parties selects an already loaded array without another request.

The flow is SvelteKit `routes/rankings/+page.server.ts` → `lib/server/rankings.ts` → Rust `/rankings` handler → `domain/services/rankings.rs` → SQLx repository `outbound/rankings.rs`. Rust owns totals, sorting and truncation. Frontend adapters preserve order, format decimal strings and produce presentation rows.

Relevant ownership and constraints:

- `frontend/src/lib/rankings.ts` owns the four options, their SVG geometry and row mapping.
- `frontend/src/lib/ui/CategoryWheel.svelte` renders caller supplied sector paths. Its canvas is fixed at 284×284 internally and each option has a 142×142 clipped native button. The current full circle geometry belongs to the feature options.
- `frontend/src/lib/ui/RankingList.svelte` renders every supplied row with an ordinal starting at one. It has no sorting or pagination.
- `exposed/src/lib/domain/services/rankings.rs:29` sorts exact GBP totals descending, with null amounts last and identity keys ascending for ties. It then calls `.take(10)`.
- `frontend/src/lib/server/rankings.ts:20` rejects any board containing more than ten rows. Removing Rust truncation alone would break loading.
- Rankings have no cursor, offset, total count or has-more flag. All four boards arrive in a single response. There is no existing sorting control or Show more action.

Date availability differs between subsystems:

- Ranking rows expose only identity, name, context and declared totals. The sole date in `Rankings` is the shared current-term start.
- The ranking repository reads declaration registration dates and filters them to the current term. The ranking service discards dates when creating rows. No entity latest/oldest date is currently defined in that response.
- Full member and funder details expose each declaration’s nullable `registeredAt`. Member summaries also expose first and last registration dates; funder details expose first registration date.
- Database members, declarations and funders have `created_at` and `updated_at`, but these are not exposed by the ranking or search frontend models.
- Search results also contain no dates. Search defaults to ten matches per entity type, ordered by matching relevance rather than registration date or name.

Separate history screens already paginate complete declaration arrays. `MemberHistory.svelte` and `FunderHistory.svelte` filter registration dates locally and show pages of ten through Previous/Next controls. SQL orders those declarations by registration descending, undated last, then source declaration ID descending. There is no alphabetical tie-break or oldest-first control there.

Financial gotchas remain material. MP rankings include all declaration categories. Individual and company boards use donation/support only. “Companies” includes every canonical non-individual funder kind. Party support is attributed to the recipient MP’s latest stored party. All current rankings exclude undated and pre-term declarations. Party rows have no detail link.

The product clarification matters because “latest” has no ranking-row date today, “entity” could mean the four board categories or individual rows, and Show more cannot expose additional ranking records from the present top-ten response. Existing focused coverage is in `frontend/tests/rankings.spec.ts`, `frontend/tests/loader-adapters.spec.ts`, `frontend/tests/design-system.spec.ts` and Rust ranking service/repository tests.
